description:
'''Alternative hip-hop''' (also known as '''alternative rap''') is a [[subgenre]] of [[hip-hop]] that refuses to be placed into any traditional type of rap, such as gangsta rap, funk, bass, hardcore, and party rap. They blur genres together and are heavily inspired by funk, pop/rock, soul, jazz, folk and reggae. Originally emerging in the 1980s, the style was spearheaded by the [[Native Tongues]] collective in the [[East Coast hip-hop|East Coast]] which included acts like the [[Jungle Brothers]], [[De La Soul]], [[A Tribe Called Quest]], and [[Queen Latifah]]. These artists used Afrocentric themes, use of eclectic [[Sampling (music)|sampling]] and [[jazz]]-influenced beats.

During the 1990s, the alternative hip-hop movement expanded with [[West Coast hip-hop|West Coast]] artists such as [[the Pharcyde]], [[Digital Underground]], [[Souls of Mischief]], and [[Outkast]]. The commercial and cultural momentum of the movement was impeded by the rise and popularity of West Coast gangsta rap, though experienced a degree of [[Mainstream radio|mainstream]] recognition through the success of [[the Fugees]], De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest, Outkast and Arrested Development. The Native Tongues movement inspired later alt-rap acts such as [[the Roots]], , [[Black Eyed Peas]], [[Pharrell Williams]], [[Kanye West]] and [[Pusha T]].

By the 2000s to 2010s, alternative hip-hop reattained its place within the mainstream through the "[[backpack rap]]" movement, which included the [[Crossover music|crossover]] success of artists such as Kanye West. Others included [[Hieroglyphics (group)|Hieroglyphics]], [[Atmosphere (group)|Atmosphere]], [[Aceyalone]], [[Dilated Peoples]] and [[The Alchemist (musician)|the Alchemist]]. Collectives such as [[Odd Future]] and [[Brockhampton (band)|Brockhampton]] emerged out of the movement, while alternative hip-hop evolved to encompass several [[Trap music|trap]]-based [[Internet rap]] genres.
